[ORCHESTRATOR RE-CLASSIFICATION 2026-09-18] Verdict changed from PASS to DRIFT by the main session. The probing subagent's evidence is accepted in full and unaltered; only the verdict label is corrected, for consistency with how this suite has judged the identical situation elsewhere.
Rationale: contract.undeclared_returned is non-empty (group_id, color_preset, created_at, updated_at), which is by definition DRIFT ('invoked, but declared and actual disagree'), not PASS ('the response carries what the contract declares'). Batch 2's get_custom_field was classified DRIFT on exactly this basis - five real fields returned that the contract never mentions - so labelling this one PASS would make the two batches non-comparable.
A second, compounding reason: the declared 200 here is a near-empty {"type":"object"} with only an informal returns hint of [id, name]. Even had the response matched, that PASS would have been HOLLOW - a contract that commits to almost nothing cannot meaningfully fail a conformance check. The subagent itself described the declared shape as 'thin/hollow by itself'. Six real fields came back against two informally hinted ones.
What the probe genuinely established, and which is NOT in doubt: the rename worked and was verified in storage (old wording gone, new wording present, count unchanged at 1), and the tag stayed attached to scratch case 1972036/TC-54457 rather than being silently detached. The effect of the write is correct; only its declared response shape is wrong.

list_tags_v3 vs list_test_case_tags DISCREPANCY RESOLUTION: re-checked both, well after the tag's creation and again after the rename. Both now agree in every check: list_tags (setup steps 1 and 5) and list_test_case_tags (setup steps 3 and 7) both reported count 1 with the tag present, both before and after the rename. Since the two probes agree once run sequentially rather than concurrently, this confirms the earlier disagreement (list_tags count 0 vs list_test_case_tags count 1) was a TIMING RACE between the two sibling probes' concurrent execution, not a genuine under-report by list_tags. No further action needed against list_tags on this point.
